This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 to 4 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 22.04.2011 at about 5.45 p.m. he had been travelling as a passenger in an autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA421646 along with other passengers at Yarabnagar, Channapatna Town, Ramanagara District, a car bearing Reg.No.KA02 ME569 came in high speed rash and negligently and dashed against the said auto, due to the said accident, petitioner and other passengers SCCH5 sustained grievous injuries, hence immediately he was taken to Government Hospital Channapatna, after first aid he was shifted to KIMS Hospital,
wherein he has taken treatment as indoor patient and spent an amount of Rs.5,00,000/.

3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 22 years, hale and healthy, working as agriculturist cummilk vendor, thereby earning Rs.12,000/ p.m., due to this accident he is unable to lead the normal life, he has lost his income and earning capacity.
Out of this accident crime No.42/2011 is registered against the driver of the said car before the Channapatna East Police.

R1 is the insurer of car bearing Reg.No.KA02ME 569, R2 is owner of the said car, R3 is insurer of autorickshaw Pradeep K M vs Bharti Axa General Insurance Co Ltd on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78761922/

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.8,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.

On service of notice, R1/insurer of the car bearing Reg.No.KA02ME569 has appeared and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioner and admits issuance of policy to said car, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.

Further submitted that, driver of the offending car drove the same without having valid and effective driving license, he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.170 of M.V.Act, claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. R3 has appeared and filed written statement denying case of the petitioner and submitted that,
petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

As SCCH5 per the complaint, Pradeep was driving the autorickshaw in question, but in further statement the driver of the autorickshaw was not Pradeep, but one Nagendra was driving the vehicle, which is contrary to the true facts.
Further owner of the autorickshaw Pradeep was not having valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.

Further one Shivalingagowda, ownercum driver of the santro car has lodged another complaint before Channapatna Police Station at about 2.45 p.m. on 23.04.2011 in respect of same accident and crime No.43/2011 is registered before the Channapatna Police Station.
In this complaint, Shivalingagowda has stated that, autorickshaw was over loaded and dashed against his car resulting in injuries to him and inmates of the car.
SCCH5 6.

Further submitted that, he has issued policy of insurance in respect of autorickshaw bearing Reg.No. KA421646 vide Policy No.67010431100100009525 for the period from 08.02.2011 to 07.02.2012 in favour of R4.

The liability if any of R3 would arise only in the event of the petitioner proving with clear proof of evidence that, he was not the driver of the autorickshaw at the time of accident, but one Nagendra who is stated to be the driver of the autorickshaw was in possession of valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle subject to R.C.book, F.C., route permit etc., he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

On service of notice R2 and R4/owners of the car and auto have remained absent, hence placed exparte.
SCCH5 7.

On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, on 22.04.2011 at about 5.45 p.m. when petitioner was travelling as passenger in an autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA421646 along with other passengers from Channapatna towards Agraharavagerahalli, when Auto Pradeep K M vs Bharti Axa General Insurance Co Ltd on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78761922/
3 came near Yarabnagar, Channapatna Taluk, within the jurisdiction of Channapatna East Police Station, at that time, car bearing Reg.No.KA02ME569 driven by its driver came to said spot with high speed in rash and negligent manner while so driving dashed his SCCH5 vehicle against autorickshaw?

marked documents as per Ex.R.3 to Ex.R.18.

Then common judgment is passed on 08.05.2015 along with other MVC No.6036/2011, 6037/2011 and 7453/2012.
Accordingly this petition is dismissed and other petitions are allowed.

Aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by this tribunal, present petitioner filed MFA No.7843/2015 (MVI) before Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, wherein after hearing on both the side, judgment and award passed by this tribunal is set aside only related to this case and remanded back this matter with a direction to give opportunity to both the parties to depose their evidence, find out the fact that, who is the driver of the autorickshaw at the time of accident and give findings on merits.

On going through the charge sheet it is noticed that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the auto driver, but looking the rest of the police papers, like complaint, FIR, spot mahazar,
statement of witnesses and medical report and also IMV report it is noticed that, there is negligency of drivers of both the vehicles, but Investigation Officer has filed charge sheet holding that, there is only negligency of the auto driver.
19.

Further in the petition, there is no allegation against the auto driver, very allegation is only against the SCCH5 car driver, it goes to show that, inspite of having material against car driver,
Investigation Officer has filed charge sheet only against the auto driver.
Further inspite of having materials against auto driver, petitioner has filed petition only against car driver.
Looking to all these aspects, this court comes to the conclusion that, there is contributory negligence of the auto driver and car driver.
20. Further there is dispute that, whether driver of the auto was Pradeep or Nagendra.
Looking to the first information given by the informant Veena i.e., inmate of the auto, Pradeep is the auto driver.
Further Doctor has certified that, Veena is in good state of mind to give her statement.
Very first information is taken at the first instance in the hospital, but there is further statement of the Veena to show that, Nagenda was driver of the Auto.
In the case on hand, petitioner/Pradeep has not SCCH5 examined the Nagendra to show that, Nagendra was driver at the time of accident.
Further he has not made efforts to examine the Veena to prove that, whether she has given further statement before the police stating that, Nagendra had been driving the auto.
Further not tried to convince that, why Veena has given false information in the first information before the police and how her further statement is correct.

21. The counsel for R1 argued that, first information and further statement are given on the same day, but there is no document on record to show that, on the same day further statement is recorded, except date mentioned on further statement.

If further statement is given on the day of the first information, which would have been furnished by the Investigation Officer before the Magistrate stating that, there is further statement of SCCH5 the first informant, but he has not made so.
Such further statement is furnished before the Magistrate only along with the final report.

22. There is much argument by the counsel R3 and petitioner that, Nagendra has admitted his guilt before the Magistrate and paid fine, so that, no more is required to prove the offence committed by the Nagendra.

Further argued that in all other 3 petitions, already this tribunal given findings that,
Nagendra was the auto driver at the time of accident, accordingly payment is also made by the insurance company of the auto. Only on the basis of such judgment it is not possible to hold that,
Nagednra was the driver at the time of accident, further all the inmates of the auto have sustained injuries, it is a head on collusion accident.
SCCH5 23.
In the case on hand there is medical evidence as such Pradeep/petitioner has sustained injuries and taken treatment.
Nagendra has not at all sustained injuries and taken treatment.

Under such circumstances, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, in order to protect the car driver and help Pradeep K M vs Bharti Axa General Insurance Co Ltd on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78761922/
6 the inmates of the auto, Investigation Officer has filed charge sheet only against the auto driver protecting the car driver.

Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 partly in the affirmative.
25. Issue No.2:

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained diffuse swelling over the right knee joint, ankle dislocated posteriorily, abrasion over the right medial aspect of the knee joint,
ankle joint and dorsum of the foot, tenderness over both malleolus, movements are painful and restricted, bimalleolar fracture of posterio lateral dislocation of the right ankle joint, for which he has undergone open reduction and internal fixation with malleolar screw for medial SCCH5 malleolus and semi tubulor plate for fibula.

In this regard he has furnished discharge summary marked as Ex.P.6, copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.16.
26.

Further Dr.H.B.Shivakumar, Orthopaedic Surgeon at KIMS Hospital is examined as PW2 and furnished case sheet, OPD card and Xray Film as per Ex.P.13 to Ex.P.15 and further assessed total disability of right lower limb at the rate of 47.9% and whole body disability at the rate of 23.95%.
27.

In crossexamination by counsel for petitioner deposed that, Dr.Channappa, Dr.Priyadarshini and Dr.Santhosh have treated the petitioner, but he has no records to show that, petitioner came to their hospital and treated him.
Petitioner condition was satisfactory at the time of discharge.
There was advice for normal walk after 6 weeks of the discharge.
He cannot say the nature SCCH5 of the treatment, further he do not know that, whether there was physiotherapy or not.
He has not seen such any documents.
Further he do not know anything about the follow up treatment.
He has examined the petitioner on 30.06.2012 to assess the disability and not given any treatment.
Further denied that, he is deposing false evidence to help the petitioner.
28. In crossexamination by counsel for R2 deposed that, he has not seen the case history.
In cross examination by counsel for R3 deposed that, there was no injury to the knee, further there was no external wound.
There was only abrasions over right knee, he do not know about the wound certificate.
Further he do not know about the admission and treatment, further denied that, implant will be permanent and which cannot be removed.
SCCH5 29.

35. It is noticed that, R1 has issued comprehensive insurance policy bearing No.FPV/S0007176/41/12/B1411F in favour of R2, which is valid since 23.12.2010 to 22.12.2011.

Very accident is occurred on 22.04.2011, it goes to show that, very policy is in force as on the date of accident, which covers the insurance of the R2, so that, R1 is liable to indemnify the R2 at the rate of 50% of the award amount with interest.

Under such circumstances, which covers the liability pertains to R4, so that, R3 is liable to indemnify R4.
In the case on hand, in the above issues already this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner himself was a driver of the auto at the time of accident.
Under such circumstances, when it is a package policy, which covers drivers of the auto.
So that, R3 is liable to indemnify R4 at the rate of 50% of the award amount with interest.

So that, R1/insurer of the car and R3/insurer of the auto are directed to deposit the award amount in the ration of 50:50 with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,09,730/ (Rupees Two Lakhs Nine Thousand Seven Hundred Thirty Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 and 3 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days in the ratio of 50:50 from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through epayment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept SCCH5 in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

So that, R1/insurer of the car and R3/insurer of the auto are directed to deposit the award amount in the ration of 50:50 with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
